summary_ja: トレーディング・デスクの設置義務と、算出方式ごとに各デスクが満たすべき組織・管理・報告上の要件を定める。
summary_en: Requires trading desks to be established and sets out, by calculation method, the organizational, risk-management and reporting requirements each desk must satisfy.
paragraphs: An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach or an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized method shall establish trading desks.

Each trading desk shall satisfy the requirements prescribed in the following items according to the category of calculation method listed in those items. (i) Internal model approach: all of the requirements listed in the items of the following paragraph (or, in the case of a trading desk that handles foreign exchange risk and commodity risk relating to instruments in the banking book or an internal transactions desk, the requirement listed in item (x) of that paragraph). (ii) Standardized method: all of the requirements listed in the items of the following paragraph (excluding item (x)(b)) (or, in the case of a trading desk that handles foreign exchange risk and commodity risk relating to instruments in the banking book or an internal transactions desk, the requirements listed in item (x) of that paragraph (excluding (b))).

The requirements for a trading desk shall be the following. (i) Each trading account is assigned to only one trading desk and constitutes a category for managing the profits and losses of trading operations. (ii) Only one head trader is appointed who directly manages a group of traders or trading accounts; provided, however, that two head traders may be appointed where their roles, responsibilities and authority are clearly distinguished or where one has ultimate supervisory authority over the other. (iii) The roles and authority of traders or trading accounts are clearly defined. (iv) A risk tolerance consistent with the purpose of the trading desk is set, and that risk tolerance includes the risk classes the trading desk permits and the related risk factors. (v) Clear reporting arrangements to the board of directors, etc. are in place. (vi) Where traders' compensation is under a compensation scheme linked to the performance of the trading desk, a compensation scheme consistent with the purpose of the trading desk is in place. (vii) A trader is assigned to only one trading desk; provided, however, that a trader may be assigned to more than one trading desk where the company can explain to the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency that this is appropriate from the viewpoint of sound management and business operation and of resource allocation. In this case, the assignment of a trader to more than one trading desk must not be intended to manipulate the results of back-testing (meaning the process of comparing daily hypothetical profits and losses and actual profits and losses with value at risk; the same applies in item (x)(b) and the following Section) or of the profit-and-loss attribution test. (viii) A document on the business strategy (including the following matters) has been prepared. (a) The economic aspects underlying the business strategy. (b) The types of instruments that may be traded and the types of instruments that are frequently traded. (c) The method of hedging, the method of identifying divergences, and the expected holding period of positions. (d) The annual plan (including the budget and staffing plan) approved by the manager of the trading desk (including the head trader). (e) Regular management information (including the trading desk's revenue, expenses and market risk equivalent amount). (ix) A risk management framework for the trading desk that satisfies all of the following requirements has been established. (a) A department that independently monitors the operations of the trading desk and an executive officer (meaning a person delegated authority to execute business with respect to the management of market risk) have been established. (b) Trading limits (including the following matters) based on the business strategy of the trading desk are clearly defined, and those trading limits are reviewed by the board of directors, etc. at least once a year. (1) Position limits set for each trading desk (including position limits based on notional principal). (2) Position limits for the trading book as a whole. (3) Operating policy of the trading desk. (x) A risk management report on the trading desk (including the following) is prepared at a frequency of at least once a week. (a) A profit and loss report (including one that has been regularly verified by a product controller (meaning a person who plays the role of independent verification of fair value calculation results and valuation adjustments) and corrected as necessary on the basis of the results). (b) A report on value at risk and expected shortfall (including reports on internal management and regulatory risk measurement, including the results of calculating value at risk, the results of calculating expected shortfall, sensitivities to risk factors, back-testing and the P-value (meaning the probability that hypothetical profits and losses or actual profits and losses fall within the rejection region of value at risk at the 99% confidence level; the same applies in Article 253-8, paragraph (1))). (xi) The following reports have been prepared and arrangements have been made to be able to submit them upon request of the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency. (a) A report on the holding periods of instruments. (b) A daily report on instances of trading limits being exceeded and measures taken in response. (c) For an Ultimate Designated Parent Company that conducts frequent and large-volume intraday trading, a daily report on the utilization of intraday trading limits and instances of their being exceeded. (d) A report on the assessment of market liquidity.
